summary: Everything specific to this board is in one large top file, demonwld.sv. It has no module for the BCU, the FCU or the video controller, and no PAL or counter-chain structure. The scanline renderer follows MAME's screen_update order: an opaque pass of layer 0 with every category drawn, then layers 3,2,1,0 compared by priority, then sprites. It also reuses MAME's scroll and position constants (0x1ef/0x101/0x11/0xff, per-layer dx 6/4/2/0, the 0x180/0x200 wrap, scroll>>7 minus offset). The only real hardware-side signs are a resistor-DAC colour table and video timing driven by the CRTC registers. The rest is ordinary FPGA line-buffer work or memory-map plumbing that any correct core would share.

findings.note: A fake 'layer 4' re-reads layer 0's data and draws it opaque, ignoring hidden flags and priority. Layers 3,2,1,0 then follow in that order with a per-pixel priority test. This is MAME's draw_background (tilemap 0, OPAQUE|ALL_CATEGORIES) followed by draw_tilemap's 3..0 loop, not a parallel per-pixel layer mixer.

495/257/17/255 are exactly MAME's 0x1ef/0x101/0x11/0xff BCU offsets. The per-layer 6/4/2/0 step matches MAME's scrolldx tweaks. Hardware would produce these values from its own fetch-pipeline delays rather than reuse emulator tilemap offsets.
The scroll register is kept as data>>7 and the global offset register is subtracted once per frame. This is the same as MAME's (m_scrollx>>7) - m_offsetx passed to set_scrollx.

findings.signal: sprite position and size decode copied
findings.note: Position wrap (>=0x180 subtract 0x200), the size-RAM pointer from attrib[11:6], and width/height = nibble*8 match MAME's C expressions one for one. The flip arithmetic (320-x, 240-y plus a 16-line offset) also matches MAME's visarea-based flip.

findings.signal: sprite list walked like MAME's loop
findings.note: Each line loops over all 256 sprite entries, skips hidden ones and walks 8-pixel cells, with ROM address = index + cell + row*width. That is MAME's sprite++-per-8x8-cell walk, clipped to one scanline. It is not built as the FCU's own scan-time object pipeline.

findings.signal: sprite offset auto-increment on size RAM too
findings.note: The sprite offset auto-increments after writes to both sprite RAM and sprite-size RAM. MAME does the same and itself questions it with '/// really ? shouldn't happen on the sizeram'.

BCU, FCU and video controller logic is all inline in the top module, behind range-compare chip selects named after MAME handlers (bcu_flip_cs, fcu_flip_cs, frame_done_cs). There are no modules with chip-pin ports and no decode-PAL equations.
Each 5-bit colour goes through a non-linear table computed from the output resistor ladder, not MAME's linear 555 palette. This models the board's analogue output stage.

H/V totals and blanking come live from the CRTC registers the game writes ({crtc[7:0],1}), so the frame rate is the one the game programs. MAME fixes these timings and lists dynamic refresh as a TODO. The register meaning still follows MAME's documented reading.
Double line buffers, a vblank-time copy of sprite RAM and a tile-RAM snapshot are FPGA resource techniques. The vblank sprite copy is also MAME's assumed behaviour.
The 68k and Z80 I/O address maps match MAME's demonwld maps. A correct core must have this, so it counts neither way.
